cells.tense: The structure you're building is in your hands right now, and you're building it on purpose.
cells.ask: Notice one truth you already know without having to reason your way to it, and let that be enough to act on before the day's out.
cells.core:
The shape of things gets set by you and it holds. People come in with a mess, a tangle of moving parts, and walk out knowing where the edges are — because you saw what was needed and said so. Nothing rigid about it. A frame that makes the next step possible, and it works because you keep checking it against what's actually there instead of what you planned.

What you can do from here is trust what you already see. You don't have to argue your way into knowing — the pattern lands, and it lands because it's real. Let one of those landings stand as the reason to move, today, plain as that.
cells.sheetLine: You're laying down the shape of things, and you know it.
cells.verb: laying down the framework out loud and claiming the ground it covers
cells.place: where the shape of things gets set and held

cells.tense: You've already built the structure in your head and you're living in a version of this that hasn't arrived yet.
cells.ask: That curiosity is the way through — go one level deeper into what you're holding instead of building the answer bigger, and follow where it actually leads.
cells.core:
When this is steady, the shape comes after you understand. You listen for the pattern underneath a problem before you name the solution — you've done it, everyone in the room can feel when it happens, the frame appears and suddenly everything that was scattered has somewhere to sit. Patient. The structure earns its place because you followed the thing far enough to know what it wanted to be.

What you're holding is a frame built for a conversation no one's had. Every fresh thing gets fitted into it. What gets you out isn't gripping harder — pick one thing you're holding and go further into it than is comfortable, follow it past where you'd normally stop. What you find down there makes the structure you have less necessary, not more.
cells.sheetLine: You've built the frame before the thing it's meant to hold.

cells.tense: You stopped claiming the ground a while back, and you've been standing at that line ever since.
cells.ask: Pick one small structure you keep meaning to build and build it badly — three days of it, imperfect, without needing it to be right.
cells.core:
When this is working, decisions get made in front of people and they hold. You say how something will go, the room arranges itself around it, and things get simpler for everyone. It doesn't take force. You see the shape, you put it down, and because it fits what's actually there, it stands. That's the other side of this, and it's available.

What's happening instead: there's a shape that wants to come through you and it isn't coming. Not because you don't see it — you see it fine. The moment to say 'this is how it'll be' keeps sliding past, and you've been treating that as a fact about you rather than a place you've been standing. Choose one thing you've been circling — a routine, a format, a way of doing the work — and do it for three days without checking whether it's working. The showing-up is what builds it. The clarity comes after.

cells.tense: You're already the one holding the shape of this, and you're talking like it's just how things are.
cells.ask: Pick something you've been calling 'how we do it' and say out loud that you decided it, and why — then let the answer sit there and see what grew.
cells.core:
The clear version of this is a place where things make sense in your presence. Someone brings you a tangle and leaves with a shape they can work in — not because you imposed something, but because you saw how it went together and said so plainly, and your name was on the saying. That's what this looks like when you're holding it in the open.

Look at what's holding around you — the order of things, the way the work moves, what people expect — and notice it holds because you decided it would. Pick one of those decisions and own it plainly: say it's yours, say what it was for. Then leave it. Give the thing you shaped the time to show you what it made. Let the building rest here and gather what's already grown.
